chapter: Playing and hearing music in Europe
title: Mike Casimir's and Barry Martin's London bands
summary: He lived with Mike Casimir, comments on his band and on Barry Martin's drumming, and praises John Coles.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: What about Mike Casimir's band? What's that like?
Well that was pretty bad when I was there. It's supposed to be quite good now. He's changed members in the band. He just started that band when I was there. When were you there?
I was there about two months last summer. I lived with Mike Casimir in his apartment for a couple of weeks. That's why I know him so well.
Did he have Tony O'Sullivan on trumpet then?
No, Tony O'Sullivan was still here then I know. No, he's joining him now. The band is supposed to be very well from people like a very good band.
Who did he have on trumpet then? Joe Lied? No.
He was a fellow from out of town. He was not from London. He plays now with Jim Young's band. He was another guy who couldn't hold the band together. It was like Keith Smith. Mike? No, Jim Young.
Mike's band is supposed to be good. I also read in the Melody Maker that I've seen him play in good places. That means that his band must sound quite well now. Like he played in Coilers Club.

No, not himself. He's not very good. Well, he swings all right but I mean what he's playing is very uninteresting. He's just banging his cymbal all the time. That's about all he does now. I guess he could play that. He doesn't. But are you some guys in his band who are very good musicians? Like the band you play is very good.
Yeah. He's good. I played a lot with him on kind of jam sets.
